pr_title: TrackballControls: Fix logical error and allow buttons modification
pr_body:
Fixes https://github.com/mrdoob/three.js/issues/26366

**Description**

Fix the logical error occuring from comparing `event.button` (being a button) and `mouseButtons.SOMEBUTTON` (being a `ROTATE/DOLLY/PAN`).
It may be also needed to do the similar change in other controls.

(By the way, what is the purpose of `STATE.NONE`, why isn't `null` just used? It would make code a bit simpler)
(Also, quite a larger suggestion -- could we move all those `STATE`s in various controls to global constant STATE, making it contain something like `ROTATE, DOLLY, PAN, TOUCH_ROTATE, TOUCH_DOLLY, TOUCH_PAN, TOUCH_DOLLY_PAN, TOUCH_DOLLY_ROTATE, TOUCH_PAN_ROTATE`? And we could then remove the first three from the `MOUSE`, where I feel they don't really should belong to in the first place)
pr_comments:
The `STATE.NONE = -1` I think it can be designed to release the current mouse event listener temporarily. 
For example, initially, we set the mouse left to rotate, but in some situations, I want to use the mouse left click to do other things, then I can set the mouseButtons LEFT to -1. After things are done, we can reset the mouseButtons LEFT to rotate.  But it seems to use controls.noRotate = true. Not sure if my thinking is correct or not.

I also think moving the local STATE to the Global STATE is a good idea. Then the developer can access the STATE value, using THREE.STATE or something. 

Current changes, the STATE is also the trackballcontrols class private attribute, so users cannot access it outside. When user set a customer mouse operations, they only can do 
```ts
mouseButtons={
  LEFT: 2,
  MIDDLE: 1,
  RIGHT: 0
}
```
Which is not very convenient compared to using THREE.STATE.ROTATE... outside.
And we also need to update the .d.ts for this class. Otherwise, we may meet some errors when we develop in ts environment.

> The STATE.NONE = -1 I think it can be designed to release the current mouse event listener temporarily.
For example, initially, we set the mouse left to rotate, but in some situations, I want to use the mouse left click to do other things, then I can set the mouseButtons LEFT to -1. After things are done, we can reset the mouseButtons LEFT to rotate. But it seems to use controls.noRotate = true. Not sure if my thinking is correct or not.

I'm not sure this is how that is intended to use... I think it's still a bit clearer to use `null`.

issue_context.title: Trackball controls cannot customise user mouse buttons
comments:
Also, I think there is a logical error in the current code. `event.button`, being `MOUSE.LEFT/MIDDLE/RIGHT` is compared to `scope.mouseButtons.LEFT/MIDDLE/RIGHT`, which is `MOUSE.ROTATE/DOLLY/PAN`. This works only because they are equal.
I will file a PR with my solution.

review_comments:
It was originally intended to align  the API of `TrackballControls` to `OrbitControls`. Changing how `mouseButtons` is configured like in this PR counteracts with this goal. So it has to be:
```js
this.mouseButtons = { LEFT: MOUSE.ROTATE, MIDDLE: MOUSE.DOLLY, RIGHT: MOUSE.PAN };
```
Wouldn't it be better to change this in OrbitControls in the same way? Currently this is a logical error (in that `switch` on lines 541-556) and this PR fixes it.

This code here will always get _state = STATE.NONE.
because scope.mouseButtons[ event.button ] will always equal `undefined`.

```ts
const mouseButtons = { LEFT: STATE.ROTATE, MIDDLE: STATE.DOLLY, RIGHT: STATE.PAN };
console.log(mouseButtons[0]) // result is undefined
```
event.button will return the number when the user use mouse buttons to click:

- left button clicked, event.button return 0
- middle wheel clicked, event.button return 1
- right button clicked, event.button return 2
Indeed! Fixed that.
